history.user: I went to a drop-in wheel-throwing class on my own this afternoon, the first time I have touched clay since school. My bowl collapsed twice, and the teacher, Ines, who had clay right up to her elbows, finally came over and had me make a very small cup instead.
history.assistant: Two collapses and then a small cup. Starting smaller is how most people get one to stand.

history.user: The cup leans to one side like it is listening to something. I picked a glaze called seafoam and they will fire it next week. My forearms are aching already, and I have not felt this pleased with myself in months.
history.assistant: A cup that leans in to listen, in seafoam. The aching arms sound well earned.

history.user: Signed Milo up for the Saturday ceramics club at the community centre this week. There were only twelve places, and I was refreshing the page at seven in the morning to get one.
history.assistant: Seven in the morning for one of twelve places. That is a keen parent and, with luck, a keen potter.

history.user: First session today. He rolled out a coil pot, got bored, and turned it into a dinosaur with a very long neck. He carried it to the car on a paper plate as though it were a wedding cake.
history.assistant: A coil pot that grew a neck. And carried with all the ceremony it deserved.

steps.text: Didn't I tell you once about a time I had a go at pottery myself? How did that go? I can barely remember it now.
